sections.sectionSummaryBrief: When Israel below issues a halachic ruling that the time for redemption has arrived, the redemption comes immediately.

translations.translation: And based on this, when Israel below issue a halachic ruling according to Torah that the time of the redemption has already arrived
(for all the appointed times have elapsed,
and Israel has already done teshuvah),
— so it shall be fulfilled, and immediately and at once the redemption comes.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The holiday of Shavuot is connected to Moshe Rabbeinu, who received and transmitted the Torah, and to the instruction to raise many students, which includes every Jew.

translations.translation: And to add that the holiday of Shavuot is connected to Moshe Rabbeinu,
for Moshe
received the Torah from Sinai and transmitted it, etc., until the Men of the Great Assembly, who said, "Raise up many students,"
in which
("many students")
is included every single Jew,
men, women, and children.
[And it can be said that the meaning of "raise up many students" is also that each one of the students
(i.e., each one of Israel)
becomes a pillar,
through whom are sustained all three pillars upon which the world stands].

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Shavuot is also connected to King Dovid and the Baal Shem Tov, and its days are especially suited for learning and spreading Torah in a way of renewal that reveals the renewal of creation.

translations.translation: And the holiday of Shavuot is connected to King Dovid and the Baal Shem Tov,
whose yahrzeits fall on Shavuot.
And since the concept of the renewal of creation is the Baal Shem Tov's explanation of the verse "Forever, O L-rd, Your word stands firm in the heavens,"
a verse in Tehillim recited by Dovid, the sweet singer of Israel,
therefore,
the days of Shavuot are especially conducive to the study and dissemination of Torah in the manner of "raise up many students,"
and that the study and dissemination each day,
and all the more so each year,
should be in a manner of ascending in holiness, and even in a manner of renewal,
for through renewal in Torah is revealed
(as above)
the renewal of creation,
that all creatures are renewed from nothing to existence every moment.
